2261.d: Placid, gentle, mild. Probably from epos; properly, affable, i.e. Mild or kind.

2389.d: Jannes, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh. Of Egyptian origin; Jannes, an Egyptian.

2387.d: Jambres, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh. Of Egyptian origin; Jambres, an Egyptian.

2704.d: To destroy, corrupt. From kata and phtheiro; to spoil entirely, i.e. to destroy; or to deprave.

2153.d: Piously, religiously. Adverb from eusebes; piously.

2833.d: To rub, tickle, scratch; pass: I itch. From a primary knao; to scratch, i.e. to tickle.

2002.d: To heap up, obtain a multitude of. From epi and soreuo; to accumulate further, i.e. seek additionally.

2913.d: Crescens, a Christian, coadjutor of Paul. Of Latin origin; growing; Cresces, a Christian.

2591.d: Carpus, a Christian of Troas. Perhaps for karpos; Carpus, probably a Christian.

2103.d: Eubulus, a Christian with Paul in Rome. From eu and boulomai; good-willer; Eubulus, a Christian.

2803.d: Feminine of Klaudios; Claudia, a Christian woman.

2451.d: Jewish, Judaic. From Ioudaios; Judaic, i.e. Resembling a Judaean.

2412.d: Suitable to a sacred character, reverent. From hieros and the same as prepo; reverent.

2688.d: Behavior, conduct, deportment, demeanor. From kathistemi; properly, a position or condition, i.e. demeanor.

2567.d: A teacher of that which is noble (honorable) and good. From kalos and didaskalos; a teacher of the right.

2211.d: Zenas, a lawyer in Rome. Probably contracted from a poetic form of Zeus and doron; Jove-given; Zenas, a Christian.

2308.d: A willing, will. From ethelo; determination, i.e. Option.

2966.d: A limb, member of a body; fig: a corpse, carcass. From the base of kolazo; a limb of the body.

2924.d: Critical, able to judge or discern. From krites; decisive, i.e. Discriminative.

2124.d: Reverence, fear of God, piety. From eulabes; properly, caution, i.e. reverence; by implication, dread.

2740.d: A burning up, being burned. From kaio; burning.

2871.d: Slaughter, smiting in battle. From kopto; cutting, i.e. Carnage.

2031.d: A word, so to speak. From epo; a word.

2420.d: The abstract notion of the priestly office. From hieros; sacredness, i.e. the priestly office.

2612.d: Quite clear, evident. From kata intensive and delos; manifest.

2369.d: A place of fumigation, i.e. The alter of incense.

2683.d: To overshadow. From kata and a derivative of skia; to overshade, i.e. Cover.

2777.d: Properly, a knob, i.e. a roll.

2301.d: To make a public show of, expose to public shame. From theatron; to expose as a spectacle.

2535.d: (Hebrew), Cain, son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel. Of Hebrew origin; Cain, the son of Adam.

2100.d: To give pleasure to, please (perhaps with the added idea of: rendering good service to). From euarestos; to gratify entirely.

2125.d: To fear, be anxious, be cautious; To reverence.

2594.d: To persevere, endure, be steadfast, patient. From a derivative of kratos; to be strong, i.e. steadfast.

2685.d: A spy, scout. From kata and skopos; a reconnoiterer.

2422.d: (Hebrew), Jephthah, one of the Judges of Israel. Of Hebrew origin; Jephthae, an Israelite.

2610.d: To struggle against, i.e. to overcome.

2558.d: To treat evilly, hurt, torment. From a presumed compound of kakos and echo; to maltreat.

2139.d: Well standing around, i.e. thwarting in every direction.

2577.d: To work, be weary, be sick. Apparently a primary verb; properly, to toil, i.e. to tire.

2217.d: Darkness, murkiness, gloom. Akin to the base of nephos; gloom.

2366.d: A storm, tempest, whirlwind. From thuo a storm.

2102.d: Acceptably, in a well-pleasing way. Adverb from euarestos; quite agreeably.

2654.d: To use up, spend, consume (as with fire). From kata and analisko; to consume utterly.

2226.d: An animal, living creature. Neuter of a derivative of zao; a live thing, i.e. An animal.

2140.d: Good-doing, doing of good. From a compound of eu and poieo; well-doing, i.e. Beneficence.

2143.d: Beauty, gracefulness, comeliness. From a compound of eu and prepo; good suitableness, i.e. Gracefulness.

2184.d: For the day, daily, necessary for every day. From epi and hemera; for a day, i.e. Diurnal.

2006.d: Necessary, suitable, fit. From epitedes; serviceable, i.e. requisite.

2462.d: A horse. Of uncertain affinity; a horse.

2287.d: Death-bringing, deadly. From thanatos and phero; death-bearing, i.e. Fatal.

2138.d: Compliant, ready to obey. From eu and peitho; good for persuasion, i.e. complaint.

2761.d: Falsely, in vain, to no purpose. Adverb from kenos; vainly, i.e. To no purpose.

2635.d: To speak evil of, rail at, slander. From katalalos; to be a traducer, i.e. To slander.

2728.d: To rust; pass: To be rusted, tarnished. From kata and a derivative of ios; to rust down, i.e. Corrode.

2552.d: Experience of evil, suffering, distress, affliction, perseverance. From a compound of hemiorion and pathos; hardship.

2492.d: (Hebrew), Job, the hero of the book of that name in the Old Testament. Of Hebrew origin; Job, a patriarch.

2406.d: The act or office of priesthood. From hierateuo; the priestly fraternity, i.e. Sacerdotal order.

2555.d: Doing evil; subst: an evil-doer. From kakos and poieo; a bad-doer;, a criminal.

2029.d: To be an eyewitness of, behold, look upon. From epi and a derivative of optanomai; to inspect, i.e. Watch.

2811.d: Glory, fame, praise; rumor, report, credit. From a shorter form of kaleo; renown.

2939.d: (often of the founder of a city), creator, God. From ktizo; a founder, i.e. God.

2900.d: Strong, powerful, mighty. From kratos; powerful.

2472.d: Equally privileged, equal in honor. From isos and time; of equal value or honor.

2030.d: An eyewitness, spectator, looker-on. From epi and a presumed derivative of optanomai; a looker-on.

2946.d: A place of wallowing. From kulioo; a wallow, i.e. Filth.

2626.d: To flood over, overwhelm, inundate. From kata and the base of kludon; to dash down, i.e. to deluge.

2741.d: To burn with great heat. From kausis; to set on fire.

2434.d: A propitiation (of an angry god), atoning sacrifice. Atonement, i.e. an expiator.

2959.d: A lady. Feminine of kurios; Cyria, a Christian woman.

2879.d: (Hebrew) Korah. Of Hebrew origin; Core, an Israelite.

2200.d: Boiling hot; met: fervent. From zeo; boiled, i.e. calid.

2854.d: Eye-salve. Neuter of a presumed derivative of kollura; properly, a poultice, i.e. a plaster.

2393.d: Jasper; a precious stone. Probably of foreign origin; |jasper|, a gem.

2463.d: A rainbow or halo. Perhaps from ereo; a rainbow.

2943.d: In a circle round, round about. Adverb from the same as kukloi; from the circle, i.e. All around.

2930.d: Crystal. From a derivative of kruos; ice, i.e. rock |crystal|.

2696.d: To seal up, secure with a seal. From kata and sphragizo; to seal closely.

2466.d: Issachar, a proper name. Of Hebrew origin; Isachar, a son of Jacob.

2738.d: Burning heat, heat. From kaio; properly, a burn, but used of a glow.

2256.d: Half an hour. From the base of hemisu and hora; a half-hour.

2166.d: The Euphrates, boundary river of the province Syria. Of foreign origin; Euphrates, a river of Asia.

2461.d: Cavalry. Neuter of a derivative of hippos; the cavalry force.

2767.d: To mix, mingle, pour out for drinking. Prolonged form of a more primary kerao ker-ah'-o; to mingle, i.e. to pour out.

2792.d: (a Semitic word) cinnamon. Of foreign origin; cinnamon.

2929.d: To be clear as crystal, brilliant like crystal. From krustallos; to make ice.

2652.d: A curse, an accursed thing. From kata and anathema; an imprecation.
